steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: It's a considerably long ride to your destination from the MBCC. We have stationed staff on standby at the stops along the route. Please contact them in time if you need anything.
After another five minutes of reminders, Nightingale finally ends the call for now.
An adult who always walks straight into danger alone is taking two half-fledged kids to an unknown village outside the city. You suppose this trip does warrant Nightingale's concerns.
Though you've retrieved the lion head, your work as the clapper slash chauffeur slash guardian is not done yet. You can't really let the two of them go on this unknown journey back home on their own.

steps.speaker: Boy
steps.content: My name is Bagley.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Bugley? Bergley? Um, not as cool as OwO which both sounds good and is easy to remember!

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: Hmph, what kind of name is OwO anyway? It's more like an interjection! My name has a meaning!
Clearly unaware of your resignation and worry, the two initiators of this trip keep bickering non-stop.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: OwO means OwO! Well, explain the meaning of your name then!

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: I don't remember.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: When I was only a baby, my parents hid me in a caravan's truck as a stowaway, so I ended up in DisCity alone. I didn't have a chance to learn our language.
Bagley leans by the car window and looks out to the boundless white sand.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: I only know it was a caravan heading toward the southeast of DisCity. My home must be in that direction.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: It's a part of the desert where grass grows. Beautiful violet flowers bloom along the road too.
Bagley stops after that. Perhaps that's all he can remember...

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: What's so special about grass in the desert? OwO can even beat bad guys on the sand!

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: Is that some fake movie plot again?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: It's not from a movie, it's a true story! It happened on my way home, all of a sudden!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: A bunch of bearded men appeared out of nowhere!
OwO clears her throat and speaks in a deeper voice, imitating the tones of the bearded villains.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Ahem, you kid over there. Right, I'm talking to you! The one with the lion head who looks super badass!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Hand over Starbeast now and we'll spare you!

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: I'm pretty sure they didn't say "super badass"...

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Pff, I'll never lie about such a thing! Anyway, I chased them away with my lion head!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Just like this, I held the lion head and stood in front of Starbeast, saying to myself secretly...

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I must become an inpendent hero!
Independent...

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: That's right! I must become a dependent hero!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Then, with a swish, a warm golden ray of light poured down from the lion's head.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: In that moment, the lion head became so light, as if it was weightless! Also in that moment, it felt like a voice was talking to me in my head!

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: What did it say?
Bagley was looking out the car window, but he turns back now, captivated by OwO's story.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: It said...
As if going to leak an incredible secret, OwO leans into Bagley's ear.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: It said, "OwO, scare them away with your loud voice!"

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: Did it work?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Of course, it's the lion head's power we're talking about! Swish! My power hit those bearded men and toppled them over!
Bagley stares at the lion head, his eyes bright with the light of anticipation once again.
Sensing the enthusiasm in her only audience, OwO immediately renders a dramatized, exaggerated retelling of her journey back to Goldionville.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: So... You didn't lie, you really found your way home with the power of lion dance?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Of course. The lion really brought me home, no kidding!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I saw all kinds of lion heads back home! They come in different colors and patterns. There are also some lion cubs suitable for a stick like you!

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: I'm not a stick! I just... have a smaller appetite!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: That has to change! Being a lion dancer is physically demanding! You must eat plenty, sleep well, and train diligently!

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: If my native culture was as cool, I certainly wouldn't mind eating and sleeping well!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: You're interested in lion dance? Good taste! Do you wanna be the prodigy OwO's lion tail? I'll consider it if you call me Master!

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: Who says I want to be your apprentice? My native culture might be even cooler than yours!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Nothing is cooler than lion dance in this world! If you think there is, that's because you've never seen an eye-dotting ceremony!

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: Eye-dotting ceremony?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: A ceremony where you draw the last few strokes on the lion head to wake the lion! The dots drawn in different positions have different meanings!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: When I was very little, I once heard my dad and his friends chant a rhyme over drinks. I think it goes like this...
OwO can't even get the word "independent" right, but when it comes to lion dance, it's as if the knowledge flows through her veins, and she recites the rhyme unthinkingly.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: First dot on the left eye, brilliant as gold. Second dot on the right eye, shiny as silver. Third dot on the brow, the lucky star is forever bright above. Fourth dot on the mouth, the world finds peace and prospers...
Amid the repeated chant of blessings, the off-roader carries the three of you through the boundless white sand, heading southeast.
OwO has turned into quite a chatterbox with her new companion, sharing with him her childhood memories of Goldionville and what she saw during her last visit.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Did you know that lion costumes come in different colors? Gold, black, blue... They all have different meanings.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Around this time of year, Goldionville is the most festive. You can see lions with all kinds of different eyes dancing in various places at the same time!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: This festival is called the New Year in Goldionville! With the lion's power, we kick out all the bad stuff and welcome the auspicious, lively new year!
Speaking of Goldionville's New Year, OwO jumps up and down excitedly in the car, as if she's really seeing those endless red lanterns and firecrackers she's describing.
Bagley listens to OwO's sharing enviously, but still seems a bit confused.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: If the festival is so much fun and so exciting... then why did you come back?

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: You went through so much and finally found your wonderful home. If I were you, I would never leave again.
The boy's innocent curiosity brings out that question you never get the chance to ask. You wait for OwO's answer quietly, but she seems truly baffled and begins thinking as she thumbs her chin.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Hmm, why did I come back... To tell everyone I'm already an inpendent grown-up now?

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: You can do that by sending letters and postcards?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Right, so there must be a reason why I have to come back...

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: Ah, look!
Bagley's surprised shout interrupts OwO's thoughts.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: Violet flowers by the road! The flowers that grow around my home!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Ah! How tiny it is! It's really there! Stop the car, little clapper!

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: We're here! We've found it!
Before you stop the car properly, Bagley jumps off eagerly and lunges toward the tiny flowers on the roadside.
Several slightly shriveled violet flowers peek out from the sand, the sandy wind brought by the disaster almost draining the last bit of life out of them.
Perhaps it's really a lucky miracle that leads Bagley here to see these flowers. After all, they're really hard to notice in this desert.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: Yes, this is it! I was stashed at the bottom of the truck when I left with the caravan. I remember seeing this flower outside the village!
This is the closest Bagley has been to his home in so many years. He's too thrilled to speak properly, scrambling to straighten those wilting stems.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: The village must be nearby. I'm sure!
You and OwO follow Bagley off the car, but stay silent. You both have already spotted the so-called village.
It's an utterly quiet ruin under the curtain of sand.
Unlike in Bagley's memories, there are no oases here, let alone villagers who work in them.
The cracked land and dry weeds are all there's left in this empty reality.
Bagley must have seen what you've seen as well. But he simply bows his head and focuses on protecting the small flowers, mumbling repeatedly.

steps.speaker: Bagley
steps.content: I've finally found it! It's right here! I'm home!
